scenes.text: Imagine standing in a breathtakingly lush, beautiful national park, knowing deep down that you could theoretically commit a major crime and legally walk away completely free.

Tucked deep inside the iconic Yellowstone is a bizarre fifty-square-mile strip of land known as the Zone of Death, where an unbelievable constitutional loophole makes criminal prosecution literally impossible.

Because the United States Constitution strictly requires a jury to be selected from the exact state and district where the crime happened, and absolutely nobody lives in this remote Idaho portion of the park, a legal trial cannot physically be held.
Since this terrifying legal black hole still exists today, tell us in the comments if you would ever dare to explore this lawless wilderness, and follow right now for more insane secrets!
